messages:
anita.k: Heads up — during the 2% canary of SDK 3.0.0 I'm seeing a big spike in streaming client disconnects. Started ~09:12 UTC. Logs show repeated proto errors. @oncall please triage :rotating_light:
incident-bot: [AUTOMATION] Incident P1 created (streaming-resets). Alert rule: streaming.client_errors > 5% for 5m. Paging eng-oncall.
sara: grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/streaming/canary?from=now-30m shows error-rate from 0.4% -> 9% at 09:12. Latency small bump too.
lee: can you paste an example log line? is it server-side 5xx or client frame error?
anita.k: quick snippet: ```[2026-02-25T09:12:37Z] client=acme-1 stream_id=abcd ERR_STREAM_PROTO unexpected header order, closing```. Seen across multiple nodes.
matt: this smacks of the header reordering change in the SDK 3.0 protocol bump. 3.0 changed preferred header order for streaming handshake. Canary should have caught it but looks like some router/edge combos fail.
dave: pinging infra to see if any LBs rewrote headers. @infra-team?
incident-bot: Automation attempted to flip feature-flag sdk_release_autokill_v3 -> ON for canary traffic, result: PARTIAL. Reason: oauth token expired for automation-runner, 2/5 regions toggled. See run-id ar-9921.
lee: great, so automation only partially executed. That leaves some canary traffic still getting 3.0. Need immediate manual kill for remaining regions.
anita.k: I can run manual override for all regions if we agree. Quick mitigation plan: 1) kill canary (set sdk flag to off globally), 2) roll back canary clients to 2.9, 3) deploy server-side compatibility shim to accept both header orders, 4) assess customer impact and notify.
sara: I'm seeing tickets from AcmeCorp and BetaBank. Support ticket links: https://support.redwood.example/t/ACME-392, https://support.redwood.example/t/BETA-884. Both report session resets and truncated responses.
customersupport-bot: Customer impact summary (initial): AcmeCorp (prod) ~1200 sessions affected, BetaBank (staging) ~200; several smaller integrations (~10 customers) reported intermittent disconnects. SLA impact: potential degraded availability for streaming endpoints.
matt: runbook for manual kill: ```curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $MGMT_TOKEN" https://flags.redwood.example/api/flags/sdk_release_autokill_v3 -d '{"state":"off","scope":"all"}'``` I can run, but need confirm.
dave: go for it, matt. I'll watch for side-effects.
matt: running now... ```HTTP/1.1 200 OK {"flag":"sdk_release_autokill_v3","state":"off","regions_updated":5}``` Confirmed.
incident-bot: Automation state changed: sdk_release_autokill_v3 = OFF (manual). Canary traffic should drop to 0%.
anita.k: doing server-side shim to accept both header orders as short-term hotfix. Patch snippet applied to gateway config: ```match header_order in ["v3","legacy"] || accept both``` Rolling to 4 nodes.
lee: can we also force older SDK routing for customers pinned to stable? If not, push rollback.
anita.k: we've issued rollback tags to the canary build; CI triggered rollback to 2.9 in all canary cohorts.
sara: error-rate is dropping in region-us-east, still high in eu-west (edge rewrite suspicion). Graph: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/streaming/canary?from=now-10m
dave: infra fixed the LB rewrite rule in eu-west. That plus flag off should eliminate remainder.
incident-bot: Update: error-rate decreased to 0.8% cluster-wide after 18m; remaining errors isolated to older edge caches.
customersupport-bot: Notifying impacted customers: AcmeCorp and BetaBank notified via email and support portal. Message: we detected protocol mismatch causing disconnects for some streaming clients during SDK 3.0 canary; mitigation applied, rolling back to 2.9 and applying compatibility shim; detailed postmortem to follow.
matt: note for PMs: the SDK version bump (3.0.0) changed header ordering for handshake to optimize perf. We missed a gated acceptance test for edge rewrites. Need an integration test against edge proxies.
lee: handoff — I'm taking follow-up for the next 2 hours to monitor eu-west and validate post-shim behaviour. @anita.k can you own postmortem draft and include timeline + automation token fix?
anita.k: will do. Immediate todos: 1) rotate automation-runner token (security) 2) add integration tests for header-order across LBs 3) postmortem + customer timeline.
dave: adding blameless notes and request for RCA channel. Also creating follow-up ticket: INFRA-5732 (LB header rewrite quarantine).
incident-bot: Incident P1 resolved -> mitigated. Duration: ~00:24:30. Assigned lead: anita.k.
customersupport-bot: Final impact note for internal record: ~1.4k sessions affected across 12 customers, no data loss, reconnects required; we offered priority support and extended logs collection window.
anita.k: thanks all — handing off to @lee for monitoring. I'll start the postmortem and ping for review. Please add any missing customer notes to the ticket. :white_check_mark:
